core.title: Design-system components have a consumer
core.given: A file in a judged component layer of the design system — the first directory beneath a design-system root, with root and judged layers located by the profile — exports a component, as the stack identifies components.
core.when: Such an export exists, or the coder adds, changes, or stops consuming one.
core.then: Each such export MUST have a consumer: another non-barrel file (a higher design-system layer, or code outside the design system) that imports it under that name in the stack's consumer-binding form; otherwise remove the export.
prefer: Export a component only when a real consumer uses it.
During GREEN: if the current acceptance needs it, wire that actual consumer to it.
During GREEN: if added speculatively with no required consumer, delete it.
During GREEN: keep only the smallest export surface the current behavior needs.
avoid: Exposing unrelated internals from a barrel to make the import graph look connected.
Counting a barrel re-export as consumption.
unless: The repository has no design-system root (self-scoping: there is no system to connect to yet).
Test files (identified by the profile's test-file patterns) and never-scanned vendored/build trees are outside the check.
Non-component design-system layers (e.g. token/foundation values) and barrels are not judged.
Only component exports are judged (non-component exports, e.g. helpers or values, are not).
core.why: Unused components still have to be maintained, themed, and migrated; a design system grows by adjudication, not by accretion of pieces nobody uses.
evidence: The current behavioral or rendering acceptance passes.
Every affected export has a genuine consumer.
verification: Disposition strict, severity 2: every flagged export must gain a genuine consumer or be removed; the finding is not advisory.

Check: a repository-wide import-graph observer collects component exports from the design system's judged component layers (first-level layers beneath a design-system root; root directory names and judged layer names both come from the profile) and flags each export that no other non-barrel file imports. Whether an export has a consumer is not observable from a single file; it needs this observer (covers pre-existing orphans, edited exports, new exports, and exports whose last consumer was removed).
The check applies to every qualifying file regardless of file suffix.

Consumer: a non-barrel file — a higher design-system layer or code outside the design system — that imports the export under that name; what counts as importing is the stack's consumer-binding import form (idiom.module_boundaries#consumer_import), not assumed to be an import that repeats the exported name in every stack. Composition inside the design system (a higher layer composing a lower layer's component) is legitimate consumption; a re-export through a barrel is not.

Self-scoping: a repository whose profile has no design-system root is not judged; a root that contains only non-judged layers (e.g. tokens or foundations) still exists but contributes no judged layers.

Never scanned: test files, identified by the profile's test-file patterns, and the never-scanned vendored/build trees of the one stack-wide excluded list (the exact classification of that list is the checker's). Their exports are not judged and their imports do not count as consumption. Non-judged design-system layers (e.g. token or foundation layers), barrels, and non-component exports are not judged either.

values: file in a judged component layer of the design system (any file suffix)

fires: A component is exported from a design-system component-layer file and no other non-barrel file imports it (in the stack's consumer-binding form).
An export is only re-exported through a barrel and nothing imports it from there.
An existing component-layer export that no other file imports is edited or encountered.
Consuming code stops importing an export that no other file imports.
doesNotFire: The repository has no design-system root (self-scoping).
The export lives in a non-judged design-system layer (e.g. tokens or foundations).
The export is not a component (a helper or value export, per the stack's component idiom).
The file is a test file (per the profile's test-file patterns), a barrel, or lives in a never-scanned (vendored/build) tree.
A higher design-system layer composes the export (composition inside the design system counts as consumption).

profileRequirements.meaning: Locates the design system's root directories themselves; a repository with no such root is out of scope (self-scoping). The first directory beneath a root names a design-system layer (filtering applied separately via layout.locations#design_layers).
profileRequirements.bunValue: a directory named design, design_system, or design-system

profileRequirements.meaning: The first-level layer directories beneath a design-system root that are judged component layers; the remaining first-level layers beneath the root are not judged.
profileRequirements.bunValue: the first directory beneath the design root names the layer: tokens or foundations (not judged), primitives, components, templates (judged)

profileRequirements.meaning: The stack's concrete consumer-binding import form: how a non-barrel file is recognized as importing (consuming) an export, including any default-binding form that counts as naming it.
profileRequirements.bunValue: a non-barrel file whose import clause names the export, or imports it as a default under that name

profileRequirements.meaning: The file-name patterns that mark a file as a test file (without distinguishing test kind); matching files are never scanned by this check — their exports are not judged and their imports do not count as consumers.
How the stack identifies an exported design-system component among a file's exports.
profileRequirements.bunValue: a capitalized export (only capitalized (component) exports are judged; lowercase exports are non-component helpers or values)

profileRequirements.meaning: How the stack identifies a barrel — a module that only re-exports other modules; a barrel re-export is not consumption.
The one stack-wide list of vendored/build trees that are never scanned and that this repository-wide check also skips; the exact classification is the checker's.

neutralityNotes: The design system itself is treated as a stack-neutral concept (the shared presentational component library; core obligation coder.design.orphan-export), so the title and why keep the term. Everything concrete about it — root directory names, judged vs. non-judged first-level layer directories, the capitalized-export component convention, barrel naming — is profile data via the v3 vocabulary keys roots.design_system, layout.locations#design_layers, idiom.design_system#component_export and idiom.design_system#barrel_module; the Bun path globs are the composite of the root and layer keys and are not stored as a single key. The consumer relationship is neutral, but how a consumer binds an import is stack-specific: the ES-modules import clause naming the export, or a default import under that name, is carried by idiom.module_boundaries#consumer_import, and the core's consumer definition binds to that idiom instead of assuming every stack imports under the exported name. The never-scanned test-file exception is bound to the profile's test-file patterns via the suffix.test key: the exact patterns live only in the profile (bun.json exempts *.test.* and *.spec.* together, without binding either to a test kind, so no other suffix.<file_kind> key fits) and the core refers to them only as 'the profile's test-file patterns'; vendored/build trees resolve to the one stack-wide roots.excluded list, whose exact classification the Bun checker owns (deference kept in core:verification). The detector id (bun_design_system_detector) and the coder.vite.design-orphan-ui lineage reference have no neutral equivalent and remain bunOnly.
